final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor introduced no new admissible evidence and expressly conceded the key unresolved facts: the affected mental health referral routing segment remains exposed, and there is no shown reviewed risk acceptance covering that exposure. That means the audit picture is unchanged from the initial report. The Actor's narrower argument is a reinterpretation of the same record, not new evidence. On the stated policy text, rollout controls and post-launch monitoring can mitigate a material weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or reviewed risk acceptance explains why exposure is acceptable. The available record, as summarized here, shows neither predicate. Disclosure in the model card may be necessary, but it is not enough to convert the unresolved policy failure into compliant or compliant_with_caveats status. The strongest evidence-supported conclusion remains noncompliant.
remaining_concerns: The mental health referral routing segment remains below target and exposed in the rollout cohort.
The admissible record still does not show exclusion of that affected use case from rollout.
The admissible record still does not show reviewed and approved risk acceptance specifically covering that exposed segment.
The policy text makes rollout controls and monitoring insufficient on their own when the affected segment remains exposed.
Model-card disclosure may be required, but disclosure alone does not satisfy the stated exclusion-or-risk-acceptance predicate for certification.
